newsitem.title: USA: U.S. magazine settles libel suit by Cuban exiles.
newsitem.headline: U.S. magazine settles libel suit by Cuban exiles.

text.p: A powerful hardline Cuban exile organisation said on Monday it had reached a $100,000 agreement to settle a libel suit against The New Republic for a cover story that labeled its chairman a "mobster."

The political weekly agreed to contribute $100,000 to the Cuban American National Foundation (CANF) for a scholarship and to issue a public apology for an Oct. 3, 1994, article about the foundation's chairman, Jorge Mas Canosa. The article was headlined "Clinton's Miami Mobster."

"The New Republic in its headlines did not mean to imply that Mr. Mas was connected to organised crime, and the use of the word in the headlines was not chosen based on evidence of any criminal activity by Mr. Mas or the Cuban American National Foundation," the foundation and the magazine said in a joint news release.

The magazine also agreed to run a correction in its next issue in which it said the use of the word "mobster" was its responsibility and not the responsibility of the article's author, freelance journalist Ann Louise Bardach. The correction also said it regretted "any injury or embarrassment that may have been caused to Mr. Mas or his family."
"I accept with much happiness this $100,000 on behalf of the CANF," Mas Canosa told a news conference. "I believe this represents a victory for the cause of Cuban freedom and for our community."

Officials of the conservative foundation, known for its lobbying strength and adamant opposition to Cuba's communist regime, said the libel suit against the New Republic and another one settled last month should be seen as self-defence and not an attack on freedom of the press.
"It should be a trend on the part of the media to practice responsible journalism," Mas Canosa said.
In August a Miami jury found Wayne Smith, a former U.S. diplomat in Havana who is now a university professor and a specialist in Cuban affairs, guilty of defaming CANF.

The foundation said that Smith had knowingly and wrongly alleged that CANF was involved in an illegal scheme in which federal grants to support democracy abroad were kicked back in the form of political contributions to U.S. politicians.
